subject: Security traffic lights — MAP close timeline, SOC 2 / SIG / DPA clarifications
messages:
From: jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.inference>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@crestfin.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.inference>, rachel_kim <rachel@redwood.inference>, kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Security traffic lights — MAP close timeline, SOC 2 / SIG / DPA clarifications

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. As requested, I’m attaching our proposed mutual action plan (MAP) and a short SOC 2 summary. To keep the close date (target: Sep 3) realistic, we want to align on the minimum acceptable evidence and any redline timelines on the DPA.

Key asks from your side so we can finalize the MAP:
- Which of the SOC 2 controls does Crest need validated evidence for pre-prod (security vs. change management)?
- Is a scoped SIG/CAIQ with a subset of control answers sufficient for procurement to greenlight the contract, or do you need the full matrix?
- Any mandatory language or data retention windows that must be in the DPA (e.g., 7 yrs archival, EU residency requirement)?

I’ve highlighted a proposed “traffic-light” approach in the MAP: green items are blocking-signoff items (SOC 2 attestation + DPA signed), amber are conditional (SIG spreadsheet + testing window), red are blockers that will push the timeline. If useful, we can run a 30-minute intake with procurement + security to walk the plan.

Attachments: mutual-action-plan-v2.xlsx, redwood-soc2-summary-2026.pdf

Next steps: can you confirm procurement’s minimum acceptance (green vs. amber) by EOD Thu Aug 6? If not, we’ll schedule a short lock-step call.

Best,
Jonas Weber
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.inference

From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@crestfin.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.inference>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@crestfin.com>, Diego Alvarez <diego.alvarez@crestfin.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Security traffic lights — MAP close timeline, SOC 2 / SIG / DPA clarifications

Thanks Jonas — quick read-through and some clarifying questions from procurement/security: 

1) SOC 2: procurement accepts a Type II report if it is within the last 12 months. Is your Type II 2025 or 2026? We need an executive summary + scope (production systems, data flows).
2) SIG/CAIQ: we generally want the full matrix, but procurement will accept a ‘limited responses’ upload for items we triage as lower risk. Can you flag which items you consider out-of-scope?
3) DPA: Crest requires a clause on data residency for EU customers (we have EU clients). Also need standard breach notification timelines (<=72 hours) and a data deletion certificate upon termination.

If these are all covered and we see the MAP with traffic lights, procurement can aim to complete redlines by Aug 18 — but that assumes legal has minimal carveouts.

Can you have your security lead confirm the residency/retention posture and point us to the SOC executve summary?

—Elena
Elena Morales
Head of Strategic Procurement, Crest Financial
elena.morales@crestfin.com

From: jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.inference>
To: neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.inference>, kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.inference>, rachel_kim <rachel@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 6 Aug 2026 08:24:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Security traffic lights — MAP close timeline, SOC 2 / SIG / DPA clarifications

Team — fyi, procurement pushed back a little on residency + wants the full SIG ideally. Can Neha confirm the answers below (quick bullets) so I can reply: 

- SOC 2 report date and short scope blurb (one sentence)
- Which SIG items are clearly out-of-scope for Crest (if any) and which we can mark as “implementing / compensating controls"
- DPA: current retention default (30 days logs, 1 year aggregated telemetry, option for EU residency via private deployment) and our standard breach SLA (72 hours).

If we can send a concise one-pager that maps to the MAP traffic-light columns, procurement said they can commit to redline completion by Aug 18. Otherwise we lose the Sep 3 close window.

Thanks — I’ll hold off replying to Elena until we have these bullets.

Jonas

From: neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.inference>
To: jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.inference>, kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.inference>, rachel_kim <rachel@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 7 Aug 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Security traffic lights — MAP close timeline, SOC 2 / SIG / DPA clarifications

On Thu, Aug 6, 2026 at 08:24 AM jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.inference> wrote:
> Team — fyi, procurement pushed back a little on residency + wants the full SIG ideally. Can Neha confirm the answers below (quick bullets) so I can reply:

Quick bullets below (ready for external):
- SOC 2: Type II completed May 2026. Scope: hosted inference control plane + production serving runtime (token processing pipelines). Executive summary attached.
- SIG/CAIQ: Most items are fully answered; a small subset (~12 rows) are "partial/implementing" where compensating controls exist (listed in SIG tab). We can provide a limited-response file flagged for procurement triage; recommend marking 3 items as amber (encryption-in-transit key rotation cadence, reverse-proxy WAF exceptions, third-party pen-test cadence).
- DPA & retention: Default retention: ephemeral request logs 30 days, aggregated telemetry 1 year, customer-requested archival/escrow options available (EU residency via Private deployment or region pinning). Breach notification SLA: 72 hours initial notification, full root cause & remediation plan within 14 days. We can add a contract-side certificate of deletion within 30 days of termination for standard SaaS contracts; for enterprise escrow we can negotiate a longer archival window if required.

I’ve attached an export: sig-caiq-limited-responses.xlsx and the SOC summary. Kimberly — please confirm that the 72-hour notification and deletion certificate language are acceptable or if legal wants different wording for Crest.

-Neha
Security Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.inference>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@crestfin.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@crestfin.com>, neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.inference>, kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.inference>, rachel_kim <rachel@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 15:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Security traffic lights — MAP close timeline, SOC 2 / SIG / DPA clarifications

Elena — thanks for the fast review. Per Neha's bullets (below) and attached artifacts, summary answers follow: 

- SOC 2: Type II completed May 2026; executive summary attached (redwood-soc2-summary-2026.pdf). Production serving runtime is in-scope.
- SIG/CAIQ: Attached limited responses spreadsheet (sig-caiq-limited-responses.xlsx) with 3 amber rows called out for procurement triage; remainder = green.
- DPA: Default retention policy and breach SLA are as listed; for EU residency, we offer region pinning via Private deployment (we can add contract language). Deletion certificate available within 30 days of contract termination.

Next steps:
1) If procurement is comfortable with the limited SIG file + SOC executive summary, can we agree to the MAP traffic lights today so legal can start redlines?
2) Proposed signoff milestone: procurement to provide redline window by Aug 18; legal final by Aug 25; aim to sign by Sep 3.

If helpful, I can schedule a 30-minute alignment call (procurement + security + legal) tomorrow.

Looking forward —
Jonas Weber
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference
Attachments: mutual-action-plan-v2.xlsx, redwood-soc2-summary-2026.pdf, sig-caiq-limited-responses.xlsx
